step-1.text: Open the boxes in the bedroom, the frame will not fit through a door once it is built. Lay every part on the flattened cartons and count the bolts against the parts list.

count-1.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-2.text: Stand the head end frame up and bolt the two side rails to it, one at the back and one at the front. These carry the bed, so the slat ledges face in. Hand tight for now.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 end frame, 2 side rails and 4 bolts.

step-3.text: Bring in the foot end frame and bolt the free ends of the rails to it. A helper holds the frame upright while you start each bolt.

count-3.text: This step uses 1 end frame and 4 bolts.

step-4.text: Measure corner to corner across the frame both ways. When the diagonals match it is square. Now tighten every bolt, firmly.

count-4.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-5.text: Drop the metal support bar in down the middle, end frame to end frame, and screw it in. It keeps the slats from sagging.

count-5.text: This step uses 1 metal support bar and 2 screws.

step-6.text: Unroll the slats across the ledges and fix both ends. Fourteen slats. Check none of them can slide out.

step-7.text: Bolt the long guard rail along the back of the bed, and the short one along the front, leaving the gap for the ladder. Both sides of the top get a rail, even against a wall.

count-7.text: This step uses 2 guard rails and 8 bolts.

step-8.text: Hook the ladder over the front rail in the gap and bolt it on at the top. Its feet sit flat on the floor.

count-8.text: This step uses 1 ladder and 2 bolts.

step-9.text: Push the bed against a wall and give it a firm shake: nothing should rock or creak. A tall bed is top-heavy, so anchor it to the wall with fixings for your wall. The top is not for children under six.

done.text: Done. Your RUSTIC twin loft bed is built. Give it a proud little pat.
